radius-xs.$description:
--- Radius scale (#1191). The three semantic radii above named values
-- 9px, 11px, 14px -- that the app never adopted: between them they are
referenced three times, while the raw literals 4px (202 uses), 6px
(138), 8px (125) and 12px (63) carry the real UI. The scale below is
the authored reality, and the semantic names are now aliases onto it.
That way round costs three 1-2px changes; the other way round would
have changed ~500 declarations.

space-0.$description:
--- Spacing scale (#1191). There was no spacing token at all before
this: 2,522 box-model declarations, exactly one of them indirected.
Named by value rather than by t-shirt size or index, deliberately --
when migrating 26k lines of existing CSS, `--np-space-8` is checkable
against `padding: 8px` at a glance, where `--np-space-2` is not. The
cost of that choice is that the names hard-code the 4px base; if the
base ever changes, these get renamed rather than re-valued.

The app's authored spacing is two interleaved half-scales -- 4/8/12/16
and 5/10/15/25/30 -- so 10px (449 uses) and 6px (286) have no token
here on purpose. Each one is a per-surface judgement in #1194 about
whether it becomes 8 or 12, not a find-and-replace.

text-75.$description:
--- Type scale (#1191). 67 raw font-size values today, dominated by em
multipliers. Named by hundredths of an em on the same principle as the
spacing scale: --np-text-85 is 0.85em. Relative units are kept
deliberately -- the app nests font-size-relative UI several levels deep
and switching to rem here would resize things that currently track
their container.

checkbox-radius.$description:
Checkbox shape (#1245). Square, because a circle reads as a radio --
"one of these" rather than "this one, on or off" -- and because it puts
the control in the same shape vocabulary as the whiteboard note row's
glyph indicators (#1248). It is a token, not a literal in the component,
because it is a design call rather than a fact: flipping the app back to
the round control kanban's `.round-checkbox` ships is this one line.
docs/design/design-system.md section 6 records the reasoning.

checkbox-target.$description:
The checkbox's hit target, as distinct from the box it draws (#1250).
WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 wants 24x24 for a pointer target, and <np-checkbox>
already used exactly that as a hard-coded fallback. It is here because
it is a column width as much as a hit area: the whiteboard note's
add-task row reserves the same width for its "+" so that glyph, every
checkbox above it and every task name line up. A literal in two files
cannot express "these are the same measurement".
